title: Early FceRI-mediated signaling (Faeder et al., 2003)
reference: Faeder JR, Hlavacek WS, Reischl I, Blinov ML, Metzger H, Redondo A, Wofsy C, Goldstein B (2003). Investigation of early events in FceRI-mediated signaling using a detailed mathematical model. J Immunol 170:3769-3781. doi:10.4049/jimmunol.170.7.3769

kp2__FREE.note: receptor crosslinking through the second ligand site, /(molecule*s)

pLb__FREE.note: beta-ITAM phosphorylation by constitutively associated Lyn, /s

pLg__FREE.note: gamma-ITAM phosphorylation by constitutively associated Lyn, /s

kpS__FREE.note: Syk tandem-SH2 binding to phosphorylated gamma, /(molecule*s)

dm__FREE.note: membrane dephosphorylation, /s; acts on both ITAMs and on receptor-bound Syk, so it is the one free parameter that touches every phosphorylation observable

notes: The collection's combinatorially large problem: nineteen rules generate 354 species and 3,680 reactions, two orders of magnitude more species than any other network-based problem here, at a per-trajectory cost that still allows a fit in about ten minutes on one core. The six free parameters are one per stage of the cascade, so each has a distinct observable it moves first, but they act in series: a change in ligand binding or crosslinking propagates to every downstream observable, which is a different kind of coupling from the parallel promoters of Munsky_Science2012. Only 400 receptors and 28 Lyn molecules are present, so the phosphorylation observables are genuinely noisy despite the size of the network. The budget is 4,000 rather than 20,000 because a trajectory costs about 0.18 s.
